purpose: Give the finite maximal-q-adic cancellation law its honest local-algebra classification, distinguish Wilson's endpoint input from denominator survival, and prevent a finite residue calculation from being read as a p-adic or irrationality theorem for the infinite factorial-gap series.

classification.significance: Moderate as a rigorous route-boundary result: it identifies the exact finite obstruction to turning a large displayed q-adic denominator into a reduced-prefix denominator, and its explicit cancellation witnesses retire the tempting one-Wilson-hit shortcut. closest_known_result.statement: Wilson's theorem supplies an endpoint divisibility q | (q-1)!+1, hence an endpoint maximal-hit candidate in the factorial-gap prefix. The source theorem instead sums every summand of maximal q-adic valuation after common-denominator clearing; lower strata vanish modulo q and the remaining cofactor inverses may cancel.
closest_known_result.exact_delta: Wilson alone gives no reduced-prefix survival. The Lean theorem gives the exact finite criterion C_(q,M) != 0, while the q=139 and q=2593 identities prove that a Wilson endpoint can be cancelled by other maximal hits. No claim is made that this finite formula is a new p-adic theorem.

claim_boundary.allowed_wording: For a finite factorial-gap prefix and a prime q, Lean proves that after clearing by the literal prefix LCM, reduction of the full maximal q-adic power is governed exactly by the sum of inverse cofactors from all maximal q-adic hits modulo q. Wilson supplies one endpoint hit but does not ensure that this finite residue is nonzero.
forbidden_wording: Wilson's theorem proves survival of the prime-power denominator.
The prime-pole calculation gives a q-adic value of the infinite factorial-gap series.
The local scan proves cofinal noncancellation or irrationality.
Prime-pole principal residue is a classical named theorem.
The returned scan through 200000 is locally regenerated evidence.
claim_boundary.open_boundary: A target-facing route still needs a cofinal noncancellation statement and then a proof that the prescribed residue class misses the associated short Archimedean interval. Nonvanishing alone is explicitly insufficient when the cofactor changes the interval scale.
